status: GPU fault; all further native work halted; candidate quarantined
known: Both ranks recorded twelve exact first-row quality cases and unchanged inputs, followed by the same double-NaN payload mismatch. These are partial receipts inside a faulted attempt, not an operator qualification.
Both rank fault receipts were written around18:30:41.774UTC; both workers take os._exit(70) from the general exception handler.
First precise kernel fault was recorded18:30:41.795853UTC, about22milliseconds after those receipt mtimes; faults affected both GPUs BCS engines. Exact worker OS-exit timestamps were not recorded.
Controller recorded gpu_fault with the campaign FAULT latch and confirmed stopped container; it did not issue docker stop because the container had already exited.
No timing blocks, completed shape qualification or model requests ran.
not_established: Faulting GPU virtual addresses were not mapped to candidate inputs/outputs or XCCL buffers, so the copy owner cannot be identified from this evidence.
The timing is consistent with a teardown/lifetime race, but does not prove os._exit caused the faults. Candidate copies, XCCL internals or driver lifecycle behavior remain possibilities.
Successful local event polling in source establishes what the program waited for; it does not prove all driver/collective internal work was retired.
structural_finding: Known, mutually acknowledged quality rejection uses the same abrupt process exit as an unexpected device/timeout failure, bypassing explicit peer mapping close, peer-close acknowledgement, export release and process-group teardown. This is an independently actionable lifetime weakness even though incident causality remains unproven.
